The most important parts of a 4x game are the mechanics, the pacing, and the balance, but I doubt you could build a game by just starting to build the game from there. I think you probably have to think about the theme in very broad terms, educate yourself as much as you can without thinking of the game itself, then try to sift out unique or important traits to the theme, and then figure out a way to fit it into a 4x style formula.

A good example is Sid Meier's Colonization (original one). The theme was "Colonial America". The mechanics that really made the game were the resource production, trade, immigration, the "founding father's" recruitment, diplomacy, pop education, the revolution event.... These were the identity of the game. The pacing is the sense that you've built something, and that playing turn 200 feels so different than turn 20, and you are continually developing and implementing your plan as you progress through the game. The balance is maintaining the focus on the theme, and ensuring that there is not one way of playing that is overpowered, which ensures that there is a variety of ways to win and gives in reply value. In Sid Meier's Civilization they had a shit ton of units, technologies to research wonders to build, but only 3 types of pops and no goods to trade. In Colonization as they make the theme-relevant parts of the games more complicated, they are replacing or simplifying other parts to maintain the feel of the game. The functionalities of Wonders and new tech is replaced partly by founding fathers. The military really only has 3 units who don't really change in strength throughout the game, though you can get better at producing them and training them.

Another good example of the "focus on the theme" concept is the paradox grand strategy games of Crusader Kinds, Europa Universalis, Victoria, and Hearts of Iron. The fundamental underlying concepts, design, and mechanics have a lot of similarities, but they play so so differently because the themes are different. Each one of those games has tons of replay value in their own rights and you can play 500 hours of crusaders kings then jump into victoria and feel completely lost.

Now, that is NOT true of the Total War games imo. They come out with all these different versions and the graphics look different, but for the most part they play quite a bit like each other just with different units and stuff. It feels like back in the day when AOE2 and Starcraft were popular and there was that star wars RTS knock off.

I'd also say that star-based 4x games tend to do a bad job of that, they all tend to have very similar mechanics and play largely the same way. It felt like propaganda bullshit, but the worst part is they had the option of playing the game as an isolationist racial purist, but it was not a realistic play option because that play style was unbalanced. It's like they just wanted to punish people who thought it would be fun to try playing that way for once, and it greatly diminished the reply value.

Now going back to mechanics, those repeated mechanics in those space games are a natural product of the theme that they chose. They could not easily have had the type of mechanics from Colonization and then just 3 different spaceship units to fight with through the whole game. Those mechanics would not fit the scale and the scope of a space game wheere you're terraforming planets over the course of maybe 45 minutes of play time.
